claims.text: POGO is a nonpartisan independent watchdog founded in 1981, initially as a Pentagon watchdog, later expanded to monitor the entire federal government; it self-describes its mission as investigating and exposing systemic corruption, abuse of power and waste.

POGO is donor-funded, publishes audited financials and holds four-star Charity Navigator, CharityWatch and Candid Platinum transparency ratings; it produces investigative reports, policy recommendations and congressional testimony, and maintains published whistleblower resources.

POGO's structural position - contractor-independent funding, a documented whistleblower intake and a direct line into congressional investigative staff - makes it a viable off-ramp for insiders bound by programme non-disclosure agreements who will not use the DoD internal channels. Reasoning: from its documented function, not from any specific UAP disclosure attributed to it here.
Referenced by the board but no dossier written yet. This node exists so the graph resolves and so the gap is visible rather than silent — see the wave-3 queue.

desc: The Project On Government Oversight is a Washington non-profit founded in 1981, originally as a Pentagon procurement watchdog under the name Project on Military Procurement, and later broadened to the whole federal executive. It describes itself as a nonpartisan independent watchdog that investigates, exposes and champions reforms on systemic corruption, abuse of power and waste, and it operates as a donor-funded 501(c)(3) with published audited financials and charity-navigator accreditation rather than on government or contractor money. Its working method is the one that matters to this board: it takes documents and testimony from inside federal agencies and defence contractors, publishes the underlying records, supplies congressional committees with investigative material, and maintains a standing whistleblower intake with legal guidance for people who cannot safely go through their own chain of command. That combination - independence from the contractors, a document-publishing habit and a protected intake channel - makes POGO one of the small number of non-governmental institutions positioned to receive material from inside compartmented programmes and route it to oversight. It sits on the board as infrastructure rather than as a claimant: an external, non-classified path around the internal reporting channels that the concealment depends on.
